newsitem.title: UK: Merrill Lynch shortlists potential London HQs.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch shortlists potential London HQs.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch said on Tuesday it had compiled a short-list of possible locations for its new London headquarters.
"There is a short-list of locations that the firm is looking at," a spokesman for the firm told Reuters, adding that this totalled "around half a dozen" possible sites.
But he declined to comment on a newspaper report that it had chosen the Canary Wharf development in the former docks to the east of the capital to fulfill its office space requirements.
Merrill is currently housed in two buildings in the City of London area, London's traditional financial heartland.
Merrill has been widely reported to be seeking to join together its operations, which were split when it bought British broking firm Smith New Court, in a single, large, custom-built building.

One site under consideration is in the Spitalfields area of central London, property market sources said, adding that the Canary Wharf option was not believed to be at the top of the firm's short-list.

Dutch financial services giant ABN AMRO has already said it plans to have its offices in Spitalfields, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell has also opted for the City, while Citibank is in negotiations with Canary Wharf for its new offices.

The battle between the Canary Wharf development, already home to financial firms such as Morgan Stanley and Credit Suisse and soon to be the address for BZW, and the City of London is expected to hot up as more big firms begin to look for large office space.
